input.productDescription: Landing page for an online coding school for children aged 7 to 12. Classes are live, small-group, taught by an instructor on video. Parents decide whether to sign up and pay a monthly fee, and the children also look at the page, so it has to feel exciting to a 7-12 year old and credible to a parent. The page explains courses by age group (7-8, 9-10, 11-12), how a live class works (what happens in a 50-minute session), the projects children build (games, animations, small apps), monthly pricing, and a free trial class sign-up form.
audience: Parents of children aged 7 to 12 who decide and pay
Children aged 7 to 12 who browse the page alongside a parent
Parents with no programming background who worry about screen time and whether the class is age-appropriate
primaryTasks: Find which course fits my child's age
Understand what happens in a live class
Compare monthly pricing and what is included
Sign up for a free trial class
avoid: Generic SaaS template with centered headline and gradient blob
Stock photos of smiling children at laptops
Primary-color confetti clip-art that feels babyish to an 11-year-old
Dark patterns, fake countdown timers, or fake scarcity
Mascot-driven cartoon look that undermines parent trust
constraints: Single responsive page, phone and desktop
Vite + React + plain CSS only, no UI kits or Tailwind
No external image URLs and no stock photos, so all visuals must be built from CSS, SVG or code
Sign-up form collects a parent's email and a child's age, so it must feel safe and clear
